subject: Rolling withdrawals authorization playbook and monthly vs weekly debit runs
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acme-corp.com>, Samir Patel <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rolling withdrawals authorization playbook and monthly vs weekly debit runs

Hi Jane / Samir —

Thanks for the productive call this morning. Per our agreement, attached is a compact playbook that outlines how Redwood will execute rolling withdrawals against the annual committed balance and the authorization matrix we propose. High-level summary below:

- Preferred cadence: weekly small debits (default) to smooth cash flow and match usage spikes.
- Alternate cadence: monthly lump-sum debit (requested by some procurement teams) — we can support as long as authorization thresholds are pre-approved.
- Authorization matrix: draws < $25k auto-approved by finance@acme-corp.com; draws between $25k-$150k require 2 signatories (procurement + treasury); > $150k requires VP sign-off.
- Reconciliation: Redwood will send a detailed ledger CSV within 24 hours of each run; settlement team (ACME) to confirm within 5 business days.
- VAT/tax handling: we will issue AR invoices per country entity; VAT evidence and reverse-charge notes will be appended. If ACME prefers centralized invoicing, that will require a clearing PO and VAT mapping for each billed entity.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you want the weekly default or monthly lump-sum option.
2) Confirm the two signer emails for the matrix (procurement + treasury).
3) Provide the PO number or attach the signed PO so we can map draws against the committed balance.

Attachment: Rolling_Withdrawal_Playbook_v1.xlsx (summary + proposed schedule + sample ledger CSV)

If you prefer, we can send the authorization PDF via DocuSign (link at the end of the playbook).

Thanks — we’ll stand up the drawdown tracker once we have signer info.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

[Attachment: Rolling_Withdrawal_Playbook_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acme-corp.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 13:45:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling withdrawals authorization playbook and monthly vs weekly debit runs

Thanks Rohan — good summary. A couple of quick clarifications from Acme finance side:

- VAT: Our EU entities will need VATed invoices with reverse-charge wording where applicable. Can Redwood generate per-entity invoices and include VAT IDs in the CSV reconciliation?
- Cadence: Procurement prefers a single monthly debit for simplicity; treasury wants weekly to reduce working capital strain. Can we agree to monthly with an automatic fallback to weekly if usage variance > 20% month-over-month?
- Bank accounts: We will only authorize debits against two validated treasury accounts. Will Redwood provide a secure bank validation link?

I've attached the draft PO with estimated committed amount for Q4. If you can map the PO number to your drawdown tracker that will help our AP team.

Attachment: ACME_PO_Draft.pdf (PDF)

Happy to sign once we have the VAT mapping and validated bank accounts.

Best,
Jane Miller
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Corp
jane.miller@acme-corp.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

Hi Jane / Samir —

Thanks for the quick turn. Short answers and next steps:

- VAT: Confirmed — we can generate per-entity invoices that include VAT IDs and reverse-charge notes. Monica will supply the exact CSV column names and a sample export by Monday.
- Cadence: We can support monthly lump sums with an automated variance fallback to weekly if month-over-month usage variance exceeds 20%. Markus will add a "fallback" flag to the tracker and configure notifications to both AP and our collection team.
- Bank validation: Please use the secure validation flow here: https://payments.redwood.ai/validate-account/ACME-6789 — once validated, those accounts are added to the signer matrix.

Next operational items for Acme:
1) Confirm the two signer emails for the authorization matrix (procurement + treasury).
2) Complete bank validation link above.
3) Sign the authorization via DocuSign: https://docusign.com/tx/ABC123 (2 signer slots, will map to PO number).

I attached a short authorization_checklist.pdf that lists the exact fields we will copy into the drawdown tracker (PO, committed amount, entity, VAT ID, signer emails, bank account IDs). Once DocuSign is returned we will schedule the first debit run (monthly or weekly as elected).

If you approve, I'll set the schedule and open the first ledger for Q4.

Best regards,
Rohan Mehta
